question: Sapna invested ₹22,800 on simple interest, partly at 5% per annum and partly at 14% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 4 years, then find the sum invested at 5% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When time periods are the same and the simple interests from both parts are equal, the ratio of invested sums is inversely proportional to their respective interest rates.

Ratio of sum at 5% to sum at 14% = P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 14 : 5.

Total ratio parts = 14 + 5 = 19 parts.

19 parts = ₹22,800 ⇒ 1 part = 22,800 ÷ 19 = ₹1,200.

Sum invested at 5% (14 parts) = 14 × 1,200 = ₹16,800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Investment = ₹22,800

Rate 1 (R₁) = 5% per annum, Rate 2 (R₂) = 14% per annum

Time (T) = 4 years for both investments.

Simple Interests are equal: SI₁ = SI₂

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Total Sum = ₹22,800
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Part 1 (P1)
 R = 5%, T = 4 yrs

 
 Part 2 (P2)
 R = 14%, T = 4 yrs
 
 
 SI1 = SI2 → P1 × 20% = P2 × 56%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sum invested at 5% be P₁ and at 14% be P₂.

⇒ P₁ + P₂ = 22,800

⇒ (P₁ × 5 × 4) ÷ 100 = (P₂ × 14 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 × P₁ = 56 × P₂

⇒ 5 × P₁ = 14 × P₂

⇒ P₁ ÷ P₂ = 14 ÷ 5

⇒ The ratio of their respective investments is 14 : 5.

⇒ Sum invested at 5% (P₁) = [14 ÷ (14 + 5)] × 22,800

⇒ P₁ = (14 ÷ 19) × 22,800

⇒ P₁ = 14 × 1,200 = 16,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

When Simple Interests are Equal

If a certain total sum is divided into parts P₁, P₂, P₃... and their simple interests are equal, then their investment ratio is given by P₁ : P₂ : P₃ = (1 ÷ R₁T₁) : (1 ÷ R₂T₂) : (1 ÷ R₃T₃).

When Final Amounts are Equal

If the final amounts (Principal + Interest) obtained from different parts are equal, their investment ratio is P₁ : P₂ = 1 ÷ (100 + R₁T₁) : 1 ÷ (100 + R₂T₂).

Core Principle of Simple Interest

In simple interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal for the entire time duration, making it uniformly linear compared to compound interest.
